findings.title: Join the new host-answer totals to the actual catalogue and zero Core header events
findings.evidence: The new parser checks present/count signs and forbids matches in absent/empty headers, but never reconciles matched+missed with the named descriptors in that initialization, or matched with header_count for this actual unique-slot table. The source C always emits matched_count and listed-matched_count; its table is unique by slot (also asserted by the C consumer test). Nevertheless the new canned opened positive is matched5+missed2 beside named6, and its absent positive is matched0+missed0 beside named6. These are accepted as coherent. boot.header_count is also not required0 although all Core header-open/match events must0. Therefore truncated/forged new mirror counters and stale Core header count can be accepted while derived output calls them coherent.
findings.action: Reconcile each host-answer row with the corresponding filled named-descriptor count (or explicitly expose listed count if needed): matched+missed must cover the full request, with the required header-count bounds for the real unique-slot catalogue. Require the Core boot header_count0 together with its zero open/match events. Correct only the new hosted canned positives, retaining legitimate absent-pair misses and matched-zero semantics. Add finite damaged-counter guards (missing/extra misses, impossible match/count, nonzero Core header count) with coherent positives. Preserve original driver/schema/accepted rows.

findings.title: Prove the requested refusal and verify the retained stop evidence
findings.evidence: Lua evaluates base(request,...) before alter in return alter(request,base(...)). A base-provider error (for example the real header parser rejecting malformed input) therefore prevents the intentional withheld branch from running. requests is already1, withheld is exempt from any altered/cause check, and the generic callback marker plus host sound data text are enough to accept stopped_at_boundary. This attributes a prerequisite/base failure to the intended withdrawal. Separately read_all returns nil for an open failure and ignores read/close errors; the refusal branch treats nil as evidence that no boot row exists and never requires the expected empty sidecar. Thus unavailable/unreadable evidence can produce an accepted refusal. These are source-traced paths, not reviewer-executed tests.
findings.action: Make the withheld mode itself record and identify its intentional withdrawal (prefer a unique cause token/count; avoid calling the base first when intentionally withholding), and require that exact cause before accepting it. For every refusal, read the expected delegate output and sidecar with checked open/read/close; require their expected empty/no-result state and propagate IO errors as setup/evidence failures. Add small guards for a base provider that errors before alteration, missing/unreadable evidence and read/close failure. Keep actual named engine boundary verification. Do not infer a successful control from a generic callback error.
